rationale: The buyer is a real, identifiable operator — someone already doing commercial LLM inference or actively evaluating $30k GPU purchases — who genuinely needs to model ROI, break-even, and tiered pricing before committing capital. That said, this is a one-time decision-support tool (low frequency, low retention), and the market is a narrow niche: only a few hundred serious operators globally at any time. Willingness to pay is plausible given the hardware stakes, but there's no direct evidence of prior paid tooling purchases, and free spreadsheets likely satisfy most buyers today. Build gate for buyer_clarity passes at 6, willingness_to_pay passes at 5, but with only one data point and no responsiveness signal, validate first.
solution_plan: WHAT: A GPU ROI and break-even calculator as a hosted one-page web tool — operators input GPU cost, utilisation %, peak/off-peak pricing mix, and operating cost, and the tool outputs break-even timeline, monthly net, and tiered pricing recommendations. BUILD: The factory generates the calculator logic as a Claude-backed form (numeric inputs → structured outputs), wraps it in a simple HTML/JS page, and attaches a Stripe payment link for a one-time $29–49 'pro report' or a $9/mo subscription for ongoing scenario modelling; no coding by the operator. SELL: Reach inference operators via HN 'Who is hiring / who wants to be hired' threads, r/LocalLLaMA, and Twitter/X GPU-economics discussions — the factory drafts targeted replies and DM pitches for operator approval before sending. MAINTAIN: Stripe handles billing, Claude generates the PDF/HTML reports on demand, and a simple intake form collects inputs; the only recurring human touch is approving outreach batches and reviewing flagged edge-case inputs. NOTE: Market is narrow — validate that >5 buyers exist and will pay before building.
notes: No build gates fail on dimension floors, but total (5.8) sits below min_total_to_build (6.5), so stage is validate. Primary concern: niche market size and one-time purchase nature limits revenue ceiling significantly.
